answer: A stake-and-slash registry makes each identity costly. To join, an agent locks a deposit in escrow and publishes a signed identity claim. Like light through a prism, the deposit separates honest actors from cheap copies: forging a thousand fakes costs a thousand deposits. Each claim is carved like ivory, unique and hard to counterfeit, since the registry cross-checks keys against prior behavior. A quill-signed audit trail records every vote; if an identity is caught gaming, its deposit is slashed and the record stays public, so the attacker's cost compounds while agents keep their stake.
